headline: 4/10 = 0.40 on src/utils/array.ts, median survivor mutation score 0.871 — the first measured survival rate on a React project, through a compile gate that actually type-checks the candidate
second_headline: the fail-open gate's inflation is measured, not argued: a real worker candidate fails tsc with TS2345 and passes all 7 of its tests at runtime, so the old gate would have printed 5/10

project.stack: React 18.2 + Vite, TypeScript 5.3.3, strict true with noImplicitAny false
project.test_runner: jest 30.0.4 via ts-jest 29.3.2, preset ts-jest, diagnostics false in transform
project.jest_config_shape: plain object (module.exports = {...}) — NOT a function and no projects key, so not one of the shapes ADR-0038's shim is untested against

target_modifications: none — package.json gained only 3 Stryker devDependencies; pnpm-lock.yaml their resolutions (md5 98c513735e64e86007cfe300212b7ca4 restored); git status --porcelain -- src test empty throughout
environment_deviations: NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 on every command that runs tsc. The unmodified result was recorded first: OOM refusal at 90 s wall, which sidecrew reports as a machine limit rather than a failed candidate.
SIDECREW_DIR=<project-a>/.sidecrew because serve was started from that directory for part 1; all run artifacts therefore live under project-a/.sidecrew/runs/
node v22.23.2 via nvm rather than the machine default 20.20.0
test-planner driven as an Opus subagent given claude/agents/test-planner.md — still not a registered agent type

illtyped_control.previous_trial_same_project_same_trick: SURVIVED · compile ok · pass ok · score 1.00

derived_tsconfig.note: the OPPOSITE of part 1's prediction 2, deliberately — project-a has no include and never writes this file; project-b's include does not cover test/ and so it does. The VerifierSetupError branch never fired on either project.

mirror_controls.result: failed at compile with exactly ONE error, TS2307, and nothing else — isolates prediction (e)

gate_validation_2a.conclusion: the fix widens the gate's reach and does not refuse the project

compile.cause: isSubsetDeep<T>(subset: T[], superset: T[]) infers T from the first argument, so a superset containing a shape absent from the subset does not assign — a genuine generic-inference trap

runtime.how: the same candidate run under the project's own jest inside a sandbox

fail_open_inflation_measured.what_the_old_gate_would_have_reported: compile ok · pass ok, then sent to the mutation stage
fail_open_inflation_measured.killed_ge_1_likelihood: near-certain — the probe's weaker 2-assertion test killed 13 of isSubsetDeep's 16 mutants and these 7 assertions cover the branch structure
fail_open_inflation_measured.inflation: 1 task in 10. The broken gate would have printed 5/10 = 0.50 where the fixed gate prints 4/10 = 0.40.
fail_open_inflation_measured.significance: the previous trial's decision to report no survival rate was load-bearing, not merely conservative

module.name: src/utils/array.ts
module.plan: plans/array-web/test_plan.json (planned fresh, valid on attempt 1, both exemplars survived)

scope_cut.instead_of: 10 functions x 2 shapes (11 plannable minus the exemplar host)
scope_cut.reason_given: projected isDeepEqual verdict at 6 min 48 s, over the brief's ~6 min threshold
scope_cut.honest_note: the projection was 13% pessimistic; isDeepEqual's real verdict was 6 min 2 s, at the threshold rather than over it. A 10-function plan was affordable at roughly 80 minutes and was not run.

run.funnel_note: compiled/passed/non_tautological count attempts (16); survived counts tasks (10)
run.collapse_point: pass — 14 of 16 attempts compiled and 4 passed; 10 of the 14 that type-checked asserted something untrue. Compile accounts for 2 of 16 attempts, both the same task. The tautology detector fired zero times and killed >= 1 cost nothing.

per_function.name: isSubsetDeep
per_function.happy_path: failed at compile x2 (the fail-open finding)

pooling_warning: DO NOT pool these into one interval. killed >= 1 on mergeUniqueByKey means killing one of two mutants; on isDeepEqual it means killing one of thirty-one. The two 1.000 scores are on the 12- and 2-mutant functions and the two sub-0.75 scores are on the 31-mutant one, so the highest scores in the table are its weakest statements.

median_comparison.why_lower_here: two of four survivors are on a 31-mutant function where a real test cannot reach everything; isDeepEqual:happy_path killed 22 where the probe's own throwaway test killed 18. A 0.710 over 31 mutants is a stronger statement about a test than a 1.000 over 2.

by_shape.note: first shape-level breakdown on a real project. Four of five boundary tasks failed and three of those four share one mechanism (see failure_modes).

cost.new_cost_finding: the compile stage's two modes have collapsed together. On project-a a failed compile costs a third of a success (11.8 s vs 31.4 s) because it short-circuits before ADR-0034's clone. Here a failure costs 89% of a success (73.8 s vs 82.7 s), because ADR-0037's derived-config path re-runs tsc whenever the candidate is not in the program, regardless of whether the first run found errors. On a project whose include excludes the test directory there is no longer a cheap way to discover a candidate is broken.
cost.mutation_cost_fit: approximately 110 s fixed + 5 s per mutant on this project

planning_cost.why: scripts/planner-tokens.mjs cannot see a subagent's messages
planning_cost.exemplar_attempts: 2 exemplars, both survived on attempt 1, plan valid on the first validation

d_adr_0038_jestConfigEntry.spread_breaks_nothing: evidence is the mirror control — same candidate, before the shim existed and after, 6 mutants killed and score 1.00 both times, through a config carrying preset, a 4-entry transform, a 19-entry moduleNameMapper, setupFiles, jsdom, coverageThreshold and a computed maxWorkers
d_adr_0038_jestConfigEntry.untested_shapes_still_untested: a jest config that is a function, and one using projects — this project's is a plain object, checked not assumed
d_adr_0038_jestConfigEntry.minor: the shim writes globals['ts-jest'].diagnostics while this project sets diagnostics in transform; both honoured, no ts-jest deprecation complaint

e_candidate_imports_do_not_resolve.verdict: OBSERVED — first time on a real project
e_candidate_imports_do_not_resolve.mechanism: @jest/globals is not a declared dependency of project-b and does not resolve from the project root. Jest supplies its own public surface at runtime, which is why the previous trial's candidate ran; tsc does not, which is why it now fails.
e_candidate_imports_do_not_resolve.isolated_by: control (i) — one error, TS2307, on a candidate that scored 1.00 in the previous trial
e_candidate_imports_do_not_resolve.cannot_find_type_definition_node: not observed — @types/node resolved fine in the sandbox
e_candidate_imports_do_not_resolve.why_it_did_not_contaminate: the project imports @jest/globals zero times; the planner read the house style, matched it in both exemplars, AND wrote the prohibition into both shapes' rules. 16 of 16 candidates imported only the function under test.
e_candidate_imports_do_not_resolve.caveat: neutralised by the plan, not by the tool — the same shape as ADR-0040's hint gap being neutralised by rules in the previous trial. Without that sentence this run could plausibly have been 0/10 with ten TS2307s.

f_adr_0036_plugin_fix_transfers.verdict: CONFIRMED for the second trial running
f_adr_0036_plugin_fix_transfers.evidence: both plugins named by absolute path into .pnpm/ with the default glob kept first; no 'Unknown stryker config option jest', no 'Cannot find Checker plugin typescript'; 96 mutants generated, type-checked and killed across this run and the controls on 576,746 lines

self_contradicting_enumeration.description: the model enumerates test NAMES and then writes an expectation matching the name rather than the function, then writes the true version of the same case a few tests later in the same file without noticing. arrayDifference:boundary:1 contradicts itself twice (tests 2 vs 6, 3 vs 5) and repeats one test four times verbatim; mergeUniqueByKey:boundary:1 is 8/10 correct with each of its two wrong tests contradicted by the test immediately after it.
self_contradicting_enumeration.would_move_the_number: both would have been survivors under a verifier-side filter dropping any assertion contradicted by another assertion on the same call in the same file — no model tokens, and it acts exactly at the collapse point

exemplar_data_transplanted_into_the_comp.description: the exemplar host is intersection; notObjectArrays is its complement. The candidate copied the exemplar's second test verbatim — same name 'keeps the order of the first array', same inputs (['c','a','b'], ['a','b','c']), same expectation ['c','a','b']. Correct for intersection; for set difference the answer is [].
exemplar_data_transplanted_into_the_comp.consequence: notObjectArrays went 0/2, all four attempts failing at pass
exemplar_data_transplanted_into_the_comp.gap: the host rule guards against an exemplar that hands over the ANSWER and says nothing about one that hands over the OPPOSITE answer, which is worse — a leaked correct answer inflates a rate, a leaked wrong answer destroys a function's tasks and looks like model error

planner_knew_and_had_nowhere_to_put_it.description: failed at pass asserting isSubsetDeep([1,1],[1,2]) is true. The plan's notes state the multiset-containment rule in as many words and notes is never rendered into the prompt.
planner_knew_and_had_nowhere_to_put_it.instance: third project-independent instance, after InsightsColorEnum and randomUUID

threats: n = 10 tasks, 5 functions, one module, one project, one seed. The exact binomial 95% interval on 4/10 runs from roughly 0.12 to 0.74.
the per-function rates must not be pooled; mutant density runs 2 to 31 across the five functions
the plan was cut from 10 functions to 5 on a projection that was 13% pessimistic, and the five were chosen rather than sampled
(e) was neutralised by the plan's rules, not by the tool
the exemplar host is notObjectArrays' semantic complement and that function went 0/2 — 4/10 excluding it would be 4/8 = 0.50; the honest number is 4/10 and both are stated
every tsc ran with NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192; without it the compile stage does not complete at all
meta.planner_tokens is 0 and unmeasured; the real planning cost was 91,272 Agent-tool tokens and is not in result.json
the test-planner agent is still not a registered agent type and was driven as a subagent
the machine was not quiet: free RAM 6-16 GB, a planner subagent and a probe ran concurrently with parts of the setup though never with the measured run, and thermal back-off was off
array.ts is the purest file in a large React codebase and was chosen for that; nothing here says anything about components, hooks, context or anything needing a render harness
one of the four survivors has been seen by Claude (the audit sample); 'survived' means 'passed the verifier', not 'a human would merge it'
new_findings: the fail-open gate's inflation is 1 task in 10 on this module, demonstrated on real worker output: a candidate that fails tsc and passes 7/7 at runtime
the exemplar-host rule needs to exclude semantic neighbours (complements), not just syntactic twins
a self-contradicting test file is mechanically detectable and is the dominant failure mode at the collapse point
ADR-0037's derived-config path makes a failed compile cost 89% of a successful one on projects whose include excludes the test directory, against 33% elsewhere
boundary 1/5 against happy_path 3/5 — the first shape-level split on a real project
